assertions.assertion: Sets options.BackchannelHttpHandler to a SocketsHttpHandler with SslOptions.ClientCertificates (SslClientAuthenticationOptions) containing the client certificate
assertions.rationale: options.BackchannelHttpHandler is set to a SocketsHttpHandler with SslOptions = new SslClientAuthenticationOptions { ClientCertificates = { clientCert } }.

assertions.assertion: Notes that no ClientSecret is required because the client certificate authenticates the client
assertions.rationale: It omits ClientSecret and explicitly explains the certificate is the client authentication (tls_client_auth / RFC 8705), so no secret is required.

assertions.assertion: Implements a custom IConfigurationManager<OpenIdConnectConfiguration> that rewrites endpoints to the mtls_endpoint_aliases values from discovery
assertions.rationale: It provides MtlsConfigurationManager : IConfigurationManager<OpenIdConnectConfiguration> that reads mtls_endpoint_aliases and rewrites endpoints, wired via options.ConfigurationManager.

assertions.assertion: Rewrites TokenEndpoint, IntrospectionEndpoint, and DeviceAuthorizationEndpoint to their mTLS aliases
assertions.rationale: The configuration manager assigns TokenEndpoint, IntrospectionEndpoint, and DeviceAuthorizationEndpoint from the alias values.

assertions.assertion: Explains that on .NET 9+ the handler auto-uses PAR when advertised, so the PushedAuthorizationRequestEndpoint must also be rewritten to the mTLS alias
assertions.rationale: It rewrites PushedAuthorizationRequestEndpoint and explains that .NET 9+ auto-uses PAR, so failing to rewrite it loses the certificate binding.
